consigna.es: Escucha el mensaje de voz y elige qué quiere realmente Kim de Dan.

items.audio: Hi Dan, it's Kim. I don't suppose you'd have time to look over the client's proposal today? No pressure, of course. It's just that the meeting has been moved to tomorrow morning, and I'd rather not be changing things at the last minute.
opciones: She is saying he can look at the proposal whenever suits him.
She is politely asking him to check the proposal today.
She wants him to move the client meeting to tomorrow.

feedback.es: «I don't suppose you'd have time…?» es una petición muy suavizada; «no pressure» es cortesía, y la reunión de mañana muestra que lo necesita hoy.

consigna.es: Escucha y elige qué opina en realidad la jefa sobre el informe.

items.audio: So I asked my boss what she thought of my report. She smiled and said, 'Well, it's not bad... for a first draft.' Then she asked whether I'd had time to check the figures again, and went straight on to the next item on the agenda.
opciones: She is not satisfied and expects a better version.
She is pleased and only wants the figures checked again.
She is angry and says so openly.

feedback.es: «Not bad… for a first draft» suena amable, pero da a entender que aún no está bien; pedir revisar las cifras y pasar al siguiente punto lo confirma.

consigna.es: Escucha a la directora y elige qué le comunica a Sam.

items.audio: Thanks for coming in, Sam. As you know, we've been reviewing the department, and I'm afraid we'll be letting some people go at the end of the month. You're one of them, I'm sorry to say. Of course, we'll give you a good reference and help you find something else.
opciones: She is offering Sam a move to another department.
She is asking Sam to write a reference for a colleague.
She is telling Sam that his job is ending.

feedback.es: «Let people go» es un eufemismo de despedir; «you're one of them» y la ayuda para buscar otro trabajo lo confirman.

consigna.es: Escucha al orador y elige cuál es su postura sobre el plan.

items.audio: Granted, the new scheme has drawbacks, and I wouldn't deny that some drivers will be unhappy. That said, the evidence from other cities is strong, so on balance I'd argue we should try it for a year and then review the results.
opciones: He rejects the scheme because drivers will be unhappy.
He admits the drawbacks but supports a trial.
He wants to wait a year before forming an opinion.

feedback.es: Concede los inconvenientes («granted», «I wouldn't deny») y aun así apoya probarlo («that said», «on balance»).

consigna.es: Lee el mensaje y elige qué quiere dar a entender Mara.

items.texto: Hi Jo, thanks for having the party on Saturday. It was certainly memorable. I found the kitchen at eight on Sunday morning and, well, let's just say the floor needed some attention. I'm sure you all had a lot of fun, and I wouldn't dream of complaining. It might be nice, though, if next time a few of your guests stayed somewhere other than the sofa, the bath and the garden. Anyway, the cleaning products are under the sink. Also, the neighbours came by on Sunday to say hello, and they seemed quite surprised by the music. Cheers, Mara
opciones: She is annoyed about the mess and hints that Jo should clean up.
She enjoyed the party and would like Jo to organise another one.
She wants Jo to ask his guests to leave earlier next time.

feedback.es: Dice que no se quejaría, pero sus ironías («certainly memorable», «needed some attention») muestran que le molestó el desorden.

consigna.es: Lee la noticia y elige qué se puede concluir del dato sobre los beneficios.

items.texto: Commuters were left angry yesterday as the train company announced a fare hike of six per cent. A spokesperson insisted the increase was necessary to fund improvements, although critics claim that services have barely improved in years. According to a source close to the company, record profits were made last year, but when asked about this, the company declined to comment. The transport minister is expected to speak tomorrow, and a group of passengers has already asked for a meeting. Meanwhile, many say they will keep taking the train because they have no other choice.
opciones: It is true, because the company has not denied it at all.
It is not proven: one source says so and the company is silent.
It is false, because the company refused to talk about it.

feedback.es: Solo una fuente lo afirma y la empresa ni lo confirma ni lo niega («declined to comment»): callar no prueba que sea cierto ni falso.

consigna.es: Lee el fragmento y elige lo que muestra Anna frente a lo que siente.

items.texto: Anna answered every question in a level voice and smiled at the right moments. 'Of course,' she told Mr Hale, 'take all the time you need.' She had changed her answer six times in the taxi, but nobody would have known it. Only her hands, white around the pen, told a different story. Mr Hale glanced at them, then politely looked away and went back to reading. Everything depended on this meeting, and they both knew it. She moved in her chair, checked her watch, and waited, with the same polite smile, for him to turn the page.
opciones: She feels confident, and she shows it openly.
She is angry with Mr Hale for reading so slowly.
She looks calm, but she is very tense inside.

feedback.es: Su voz y su sonrisa parecen tranquilas, pero las manos tensas y los gestos nerviosos delatan lo que siente por dentro.

consigna.es: Lee el resumen y elige la conclusión más prudente.

items.texto: This study examined whether short daily reading sessions improve concentration. Sixty participants were randomly divided into two groups. One group read for twenty minutes a day for a month, while the control group did not. The reading group scored slightly higher on a concentration test. However, the sample was small and the difference was not large, so the results may indicate a benefit rather than prove one. Further research is needed to find out whether the effect lasts, and to check the results with a much larger and more varied group of people.
opciones: The study proves that reading helps, although the effect is small.
The study points to a possible benefit, but does not prove it.
The study found no real difference, so reading does not help.

feedback.es: La diferencia fue pequeña y la muestra limitada: solo se puede hablar de un posible beneficio; afirmar que está probado exagera y negar todo efecto ignora que el grupo puntuó algo más.

consigna.es: Elige la frase que dice que Leo actúa así ahora, aunque no sea su carácter.

items.texto: Everyone knows Leo as a patient, easy-going man, so his mood this week has surprised us.

feedback.es: «Is being + adjetivo» señala una conducta pasajera y fuera de lo normal; «is», «tends to be» y «by nature» describen el carácter o un hábito.

consigna.es: Completa con la coletilla con la que Leo muestra que no le cree.

items.texto: Mia: I repaired the car myself. Leo: Oh, you repaired it yourself, ___?

feedback.es: Una coletilla de la misma polaridad que la frase afirmativa («did you») suena a duda o burla; «didn't you» pediría confirmar un dato.

consigna.es: Completa la frase con la estructura formal de medio o consecuencia.

items.texto: The council has introduced a scheme ___ drivers pay a fee to enter the centre.

feedback.es: «Whereby» introduce una cláusula que explica cómo funciona un sistema («whereby drivers pay…»); los otros no se usan así.

consigna.es: Lee el titular y elige lo que significa.

items.texto: Council to close town pool after safety probe
opciones: The council is going to close the pool.
The council closed the pool a week ago.
The council has decided to keep the pool open.

feedback.es: En los titulares, «sujeto + to + verbo» anuncia algo previsto: el ayuntamiento cerrará la piscina, pero aún no ha ocurrido.

consigna.es: Elige la expresión que completa el texto formal.

items.texto: Written down, all those reduced forms can ___ careless in a formal email.

feedback.es: «Come across as» significa dar la impresión de ser algo; las otras opciones no admiten un adjetivo a continuación.

consigna.es: Elige el verbo correcto para quien deduce algo.

items.texto: I ___ from his silence that he was unhappy, though he never said so.

feedback.es: «Infer» es deducir a partir de pistas; «imply» o «hint» los usa quien da a entender algo, no quien lo deduce.

consigna.es: Elige el adjetivo para una afirmación demasiado general y sin pruebas.

items.texto: The writer makes a ___ statement, 'everyone hates mornings', and offers no evidence.

feedback.es: «Sweeping» describe una afirmación demasiado amplia y sin pruebas, como «todo el mundo odia las mañanas».

consigna.es: Completa la expresión sobre mantener una postura bajo presión.

items.texto: When the manager pushed back, Lena refused to change her view and ___ her ground.

feedback.es: «Hold your ground» es mantener tu postura sin ceder ante la presión.

consigna.es: Un amigo propone un viaje caro. Recházalo con tacto en 3 o 4 frases y propón algo.

items.respuesta: Thanks for the idea, it sounds lovely. I'm afraid the budget is tight this month, so I'd rather not go. Perhaps we could spend a weekend in the city instead? I hope you don't mind.
aceptadas: Thank you for asking, it sounds great. I'm sorry, but I would rather not go because money is tight. How about a day at the beach instead? I hope that works for you.
That is very kind of you, but I am afraid I can't afford it this month. Would you be up for something cheaper, like a picnic by the river? I would still love to see you.

feedback.es: Agradece, rechaza con atenuadores («I'm afraid», «I'd rather not») y ofrece una alternativa concreta con «we could» o «how about».

consigna.es: Un compañero dice que todos deberían teletrabajar. Concede un punto y defiende tu postura.

items.respuesta: It is true that working from home saves time and money. Nevertheless, I still believe that the office is better for teamwork, because ideas spread faster when people meet. On balance, a few days at home seems the best solution.
aceptadas: I take your point that working from home is comfortable. However, I think the office is better for learning, and I wouldn't deny that some people work better alone. In my view, a mix of both works best.

Granted, remote work saves commuting time. That said, the office is better for teamwork, because ideas spread faster when people meet, so I would argue that everyone should come in at least twice a week.

feedback.es: Concede un punto con «it is true» o «I take your point», contrasta con «however» o «that said» y defiende tu postura con «I believe» o «I would argue».

notes: Escucha: los 4 ítems evalúan implicación/postura (petición muy indirecta, atenuación de crítica, eufemismo «let go», concesión + apoyo). escucha.1 era detalle literal (nivel N7): reescrito. escucha.2 ya no resume la conclusión en el audio.

lectura.2 preguntaba un dato literal («not confirmed»): ahora exige interpretar «declined to comment» y fuente única. lectura.3 tenía emoción explícita: ahora contraste apariencia/sentimiento. lectura.4: distractores moderados («proves… small») en lugar de extremos.

gramatica.1 («is being»): se quitó el distractor «used to be» y el pasaje ya no contiene «this week he seems different»; 4 opciones gramaticales y plausibles, solo una marca conducta pasajera. gramatica.2: contexto de diálogo, sin cita de la mecánica en la consigna. gramatica.4 (deny + -ing) era contenido de N7: sustituido por gramática de titulares (to + verbo = futuro, clase 62).
vocabulario.4: «gave her ground» sustituye a «kept» (posible segunda respuesta defendible).

escritura: rúbricas ampliadas (la app exige TODOS los grupos): variantes naturales de agradecimiento, rechazo atenuado, alternativa, concesión, contraste (enumeradas por la regla de 2+ palabras) y postura; añadidas aceptadas. La escritura discrimina poco N7/N8 (P2, aceptado; es omitible).
